topics.label: Welcome and Lecture Framing
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the lecture framework, key learning outcomes, and core concepts of cancer evolution and microenvironmental interactions.

topics.label: Genetic and Epigenetic Mechanisms in Clonal Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how both Darwinian selection of driver mutations and non-mutational epigenetic alterations drive clonal fitness and malignant progression.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Cancer Stem Cell Models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cellular hierarchy of cancer initiation, comparing stochastic and stem cell models across leukemias and colorectal cancers.

topics.label: Environmental Promoters and Inflammatory Signaling in Tumor Initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic environmental promoters and inflammatory signaling pathways cooperate with genetic mutations to induce stem-like states and drive tumor formation.

topics.label: Tumor Microenvironment Dependency, Spatial Profiling, and Evolutionary Synthesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the ongoing dependency of tumors on their cellular microenvironment, the analytical methods used to map these interactions, and the overarching coevolutionary model of cancer progression.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with brief closing remarks and an announcement of the upcoming session on therapy.
